body:
### Husky 
Husky is a local pre-commit hook that will be triggered everything you make a commit locally. 
In this PR I've set it to run `pnpm run lint` every time you commit, if lint fails, the commit fails as well.

Husky is being used in most major repos including webpack, angular, rollup and a lot more. So I thought this would be a nice addition to this repo as well.

[Link to Husky GitHub repo](https://github.com/typicode/husky)

body:
# RSE-182 Fix: SCM Options in Job Menu Not Loading
When user don't have permission to scm key or password, the job action dropdown list is not rendering properly.

# The Problem
A request is made to the ScheduledExecutionController to retrieve from SCM integrations info about the jobs covered by them, so if the user don't have the right credentials, the request can't be performed and the controller was not smart enough to handle this.

# The Fix
Checking if the user has the credentials to perform the request to the integrations before we send them.

# Exhibits
Unauthorized - Not rendering options

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [typing-extensions](https://pypi.org/project/typing-extensions) from **3.7.2** to **4.6.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.6.3
   ```
   - Fix a regression introduced in v4.6.0 in the implementation of
  runtime-checkable protocols. The regression meant
  that doing `class Foo(X, typing_extensions.Protocol)`, where `X` was a class that
  had `abc.ABCMeta` as its metaclass, would then cause subsequent
  `isinstance(1, X)` calls to erroneously raise `TypeError`. Patch by
  Alex Waygood (backporting the CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/105152).
- Sync the repository's LICENSE file with that of CPython.
  `typing_extensions` is distributed under the same license as
  CPython itself.
- Skip a problematic test on Python 3.12.0b1. The test fails on 3.12.0b1 due to
  a bug in CPython, which will be fixed in 3.12.0b2. The
  `typing_extensions` test suite now passes on 3.12.0b1.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.2
   ```
   - Fix use of `deprecated` on classes with `__new__` but no `__init__`.
  Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Fix regression in version 4.6.1 where comparing a generic class against a
  runtime-checkable protocol using `isinstance()` would cause `AttributeError`
  to be raised if using Python 3.7.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.1
   ```
   - Change deprecated `runtime` to formal API `runtime_checkable` in the error
  message. Patch by Xuehai Pan.
- Fix regression in 4.6.0 where attempting to define a `Protocol` that was
  generic over a `ParamSpec` or a `TypeVarTuple` would cause `TypeError` to be
  raised. Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.0
   ```
   - `typing_extensions` is now documented at
  https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.Buffer`, a marker class for buffer types, as proposed
  by PEP 688. Equivalent to `collections.abc.Buffer` in Python 3.12. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport two CPython PRs fixing various issues with `typing.Literal`:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23294 and
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23383. Both CPython PRs were
  originally by Yurii Karabas, and both were backported to Python >=3.9.1, but
  no earlier. Patch by Alex Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the changes is that equality comparisons of `Literal`
  objects will now raise a `TypeError` if one of the `Literal` objects being
  compared has a mutable parameter. (Using mutable parameters with `Literal` is
  not supported by PEP 586 or by any major static type checkers.)
- `Literal` is now reimplemented on all Python versions <= 3.10.0. The
  `typing_extensions` version does not suffer from the bug that was fixed in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/29334. (The CPython bugfix was
  backported to CPython 3.10.1 and 3.9.8, but no earlier.)
- Backport [CPython PR 26067](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/26067)
  (originally by Yurii Karabas), ensuring that `isinstance()` calls on
  protocols raise `TypeError` when the protocol is not decorated with
  `runtime_checkable`. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport several significant performance improvements to runtime-checkable
  protocols that have been made in Python 3.12 (see
  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/74690 for details). Patch by Alex
  Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the performance improvements is that the members of
  a runtime-checkable protocol are now considered “frozen” at runtime as soon
  as the class has been created. Monkey-patching attributes onto a
  runtime-checkable protocol will still work, but will have no impact on
  `isinstance()` checks comparing objects to the protocol. See
  ["What's New in Python 3.12"](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#typing)
  for more details.
- `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable protocols now use
  `inspect.getattr_static()` rather than `hasattr()` to lookup whether
  attributes exist (backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103034).
  This means that descriptors and `__getattr__` methods are no longer
  unexpectedly evaluated during `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable
  protocols. However, it may also mean that some objects which used to be
  considered instances of a runtime-checkable protocol on older versions of
  `typing_extensions` may no longer be considered instances of that protocol
  using the new release, and vice versa. Most users are unlikely to be affected
  by this change. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport the ability to define `__init__` methods on Protocol classes, a
  change made in Python 3.11 (originally implemented in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/31628 by Adrian Garcia Badaracco).
  Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Speedup `isinstance(3, typing_extensions.SupportsIndex)` by >10x on Python
  <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `typing_extensions` versions of `SupportsInt`, `SupportsFloat`,
  `SupportsComplex`, `SupportsBytes`, `SupportsAbs` and `SupportsRound`. These
  have the same semantics as the versions from the `typing` module, but
  `isinstance()` checks against the `typing_extensions` versions are >10x faster
  at runtime on Python <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `__orig_bases__` to non-generic TypedDicts, call-based TypedDicts, and
  call-based NamedTuples. Other TypedDicts and NamedTuples already had the attribute.
  Patch by Adrian Garcia Badaracco.
- Add `typing_extensions.get_original_bases`, a backport of
  [`types.get_original_bases`](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/types.html#types.get_original_bases),
  introduced in Python 3.12 (CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/101827, originally by James
  Hilton-Balfe). Patch by Alex Waygood.

  This function should always produce correct results when called on classes
  constructed using features from `typing_extensions`. However, it may
  produce incorrect results when called on some `NamedTuple` or `TypedDict`
  classes that use `typing.{NamedTuple,TypedDict}` on Python <=3.11.
- Constructing a call-based `TypedDict` using keyword arguments for the fields
  now causes a `DeprecationWarning` to be emitted. This matches the behaviour
  of `typing.TypedDict` on 3.11 and 3.12.
- Backport the implementation of `NewType` from 3.10 (where it is implemented
  as a class rather than a function). This allows user-defined `NewType`s to be
  pickled. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Fix tests and import on Python 3.12, where `typing.TypeVar` can no longer be
  subclassed. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.TypeAliasType`, a backport of `typing.TypeAliasType`
  from PEP 695. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport changes to the repr of `typing.Unpack` that were made in order to
  implement [PEP 692](https://peps.python.org/pep-0692/) (backport of
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/104048). Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.5.0
   ```
   - Runtime support for PEP 702, adding `typing_extensions.deprecated`. Patch
  by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add better default value for TypeVar `default` parameter, PEP 696. Enables
  runtime check if `None` was passed as default. Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- The `typing_extensions.override` decorator now sets the `.__override__`
  attribute. Patch by Steven Troxler.
- Fix `get_type_hints()` on cross-module inherited `TypedDict` in 3.9 and 3.10.
  Patch by Carl Meyer.
- Add `frozen_default` parameter on `dataclass_transform`. Patch by Erik De Bonte.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.4.0
   ```
   - Add `typing_extensions.Any` a backport of python 3.11's Any class which is
  subclassable at runtime. (backport from python/cpython31841, by Shantanu
  and Jelle Zijlstra). Patch by James Hilton-Balfe (Gobot1234).
- Add initial support for TypeVarLike `default` parameter, PEP 696.
  Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- Runtime support for PEP 698, adding `typing_extensions.override`. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add the `infer_variance` parameter to `TypeVar`

author: anmonteiro
body: Bindings for OpenSSL - Project page: https://github.com/savonet/ocaml-ssl ##### CHANGES: - Raise an error when `Ssl.flush` isn't successful (savonet/ocaml-ssl#104, savonet/ocaml-ssl#120) - Add an API-compatible `Ssl.Runtime_lock` module. The functions in this module don't release the OCaml runtime lock. While they don't allow other OCaml threads to run concurrently, they don't perform any copying in the underlying data, leading certain workloads to be faster than their counterparts that release the lock. (savonet/ocaml-ssl#106) - Guarantee `Ssl.output_string` writes the whole string by retrying the operation with unwritten bytes (savonet/ocaml-ssl#103, savonet/ocaml-ssl#116) - Fix calls in C stubs that need to call `ERR_clear_error` before the underlying OpenSSL call (savonet/ocaml-ssl#118) - Add a module `Ssl.Error` to retrieve OpenSSL errors in a structured way (savonet/ocaml-ssl#119) - Deprecate Ssl.{SSLv23,SSLv3,TLSv1,TLSv1_1}, which were were formally deprecated in March 2021 and earlier (savonet/ocaml-ssl#115).

author: joshuatf
body: ### Submission Review Guidelines: - I have followed the [WooCommerce Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [WordPress Coding Standards](https://make.wordpress.org/core/handbook/best-practices/coding-standards/). - I have checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/pulls) for the same update/change. - I have reviewed my code for [security best practices](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/). - Following the above guidelines will result in quick merges and clear and detailed feedback when appropriate. ### Changes proposed in this Pull Request: Adds undo/redo buttons and an editor history state handler to the iframe editor. I originally attempted to do this with the default undo/redo behavior in Gutenberg, however I ran into 2 blockers that prevented this and led to a custom solution: 1. The entity data store needs an entity to be hooked up. Since this editor is for a piece of an entity (the description of a product), it is not tied to a specific entity. Attempting to hook it up to an entity provider will place the entire entity template inside the iframe editor. 2. There's also the `core/editor` store which does not need to be coupled with an entity, but this selects and dispatches to the `core/data` store. I had assumed that creating a `core/editor` subregistry would work, but since this just handles history from `core/data` it does not help unless we can also create a subregistry of that store. That store's config does not seem to be exposed which ultimately led to being blocked from using the GB data stores for this. Closes #38488 . ### How to test the changes in this Pull Request: Using the [WooCommerce Testing Instructions Guide](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/wiki/Writing-high-quality-testing-instructions), include your detailed testing instructions: 1. Enable the new product block editor under WooCommerce -> Settings -> Advanced -> Features. 2. Navigate to the Add product page 3. Open the iframe editor by clicking "Add description" under the General tab. 4. Note that the undo/redo buttons are disabled since no changes have yet been made 5. Make some changes and note the undo button is now enabled 6. Attempt to undo/redo edits made (note that the exact state of a persistent edit is determined by Gutenberg's `onChange` callback and does not always seem expected, but that is outside the scope of this PR). 7. After undoing some behavior, make some new edits and note that the redo button is no longer enabled 8. Optionally, make over 50 persistent edits (or manually turn this value down in `DEFAULT_MAX_HISTORY`) and note that you cannot undo beyond 50 edits ago

This PR updates [typing-extensions](https://pypi.org/project/typing-extensions) from **4.1.1** to **4.6.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.6.3
   ```
   - Fix a regression introduced in v4.6.0 in the implementation of
  runtime-checkable protocols. The regression meant
  that doing `class Foo(X, typing_extensions.Protocol)`, where `X` was a class that
  had `abc.ABCMeta` as its metaclass, would then cause subsequent
  `isinstance(1, X)` calls to erroneously raise `TypeError`. Patch by
  Alex Waygood (backporting the CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/105152).
- Sync the repository's LICENSE file with that of CPython.
  `typing_extensions` is distributed under the same license as
  CPython itself.
- Skip a problematic test on Python 3.12.0b1. The test fails on 3.12.0b1 due to
  a bug in CPython, which will be fixed in 3.12.0b2. The
  `typing_extensions` test suite now passes on 3.12.0b1.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.2
   ```
   - Fix use of `deprecated` on classes with `__new__` but no `__init__`.
  Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Fix regression in version 4.6.1 where comparing a generic class against a
  runtime-checkable protocol using `isinstance()` would cause `AttributeError`
  to be raised if using Python 3.7.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.1
   ```
   - Change deprecated `runtime` to formal API `runtime_checkable` in the error
  message. Patch by Xuehai Pan.
- Fix regression in 4.6.0 where attempting to define a `Protocol` that was
  generic over a `ParamSpec` or a `TypeVarTuple` would cause `TypeError` to be
  raised. Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.0
   ```
   - `typing_extensions` is now documented at
  https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.Buffer`, a marker class for buffer types, as proposed
  by PEP 688. Equivalent to `collections.abc.Buffer` in Python 3.12. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport two CPython PRs fixing various issues with `typing.Literal`:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23294 and
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23383. Both CPython PRs were
  originally by Yurii Karabas, and both were backported to Python >=3.9.1, but
  no earlier. Patch by Alex Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the changes is that equality comparisons of `Literal`
  objects will now raise a `TypeError` if one of the `Literal` objects being
  compared has a mutable parameter. (Using mutable parameters with `Literal` is
  not supported by PEP 586 or by any major static type checkers.)
- `Literal` is now reimplemented on all Python versions <= 3.10.0. The
  `typing_extensions` version does not suffer from the bug that was fixed in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/29334. (The CPython bugfix was
  backported to CPython 3.10.1 and 3.9.8, but no earlier.)
- Backport [CPython PR 26067](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/26067)
  (originally by Yurii Karabas), ensuring that `isinstance()` calls on
  protocols raise `TypeError` when the protocol is not decorated with
  `runtime_checkable`. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport several significant performance improvements to runtime-checkable
  protocols that have been made in Python 3.12 (see
  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/74690 for details). Patch by Alex
  Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the performance improvements is that the members of
  a runtime-checkable protocol are now considered “frozen” at runtime as soon
  as the class has been created. Monkey-patching attributes onto a
  runtime-checkable protocol will still work, but will have no impact on
  `isinstance()` checks comparing objects to the protocol. See
  ["What's New in Python 3.12"](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#typing)
  for more details.
- `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable protocols now use
  `inspect.getattr_static()` rather than `hasattr()` to lookup whether
  attributes exist (backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103034).
  This means that descriptors and `__getattr__` methods are no longer
  unexpectedly evaluated during `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable
  protocols. However, it may also mean that some objects which used to be
  considered instances of a runtime-checkable protocol on older versions of
  `typing_extensions` may no longer be considered instances of that protocol
  using the new release, and vice versa. Most users are unlikely to be affected
  by this change. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport the ability to define `__init__` methods on Protocol classes, a
  change made in Python 3.11 (originally implemented in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/31628 by Adrian Garcia Badaracco).
  Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Speedup `isinstance(3, typing_extensions.SupportsIndex)` by >10x on Python
  <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `typing_extensions` versions of `SupportsInt`, `SupportsFloat`,
  `SupportsComplex`, `SupportsBytes`, `SupportsAbs` and `SupportsRound`. These
  have the same semantics as the versions from the `typing` module, but
  `isinstance()` checks against the `typing_extensions` versions are >10x faster
  at runtime on Python <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `__orig_bases__` to non-generic TypedDicts, call-based TypedDicts, and
  call-based NamedTuples. Other TypedDicts and NamedTuples already had the attribute.
  Patch by Adrian Garcia Badaracco.
- Add `typing_extensions.get_original_bases`, a backport of
  [`types.get_original_bases`](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/types.html#types.get_original_bases),
  introduced in Python 3.12 (CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/101827, originally by James
  Hilton-Balfe). Patch by Alex Waygood.

  This function should always produce correct results when called on classes
  constructed using features from `typing_extensions`. However, it may
  produce incorrect results when called on some `NamedTuple` or `TypedDict`
  classes that use `typing.{NamedTuple,TypedDict}` on Python <=3.11.
- Constructing a call-based `TypedDict` using keyword arguments for the fields
  now causes a `DeprecationWarning` to be emitted. This matches the behaviour
  of `typing.TypedDict` on 3.11 and 3.12.
- Backport the implementation of `NewType` from 3.10 (where it is implemented
  as a class rather than a function). This allows user-defined `NewType`s to be
  pickled. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Fix tests and import on Python 3.12, where `typing.TypeVar` can no longer be
  subclassed. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.TypeAliasType`, a backport of `typing.TypeAliasType`
  from PEP 695. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport changes to the repr of `typing.Unpack` that were made in order to
  implement [PEP 692](https://peps.python.org/pep-0692/) (backport of
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/104048). Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.5.0
   ```
   - Runtime support for PEP 702, adding `typing_extensions.deprecated`. Patch
  by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add better default value for TypeVar `default` parameter, PEP 696. Enables
  runtime check if `None` was passed as default. Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- The `typing_extensions.override` decorator now sets the `.__override__`
  attribute. Patch by Steven Troxler.
- Fix `get_type_hints()` on cross-module inherited `TypedDict` in 3.9 and 3.10.
  Patch by Carl Meyer.
- Add `frozen_default` parameter on `dataclass_transform`. Patch by Erik De Bonte.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.4.0
   ```
   - Add `typing_extensions.Any` a backport of python 3.11's Any class which is
  subclassable at runtime. (backport from python/cpython31841, by Shantanu
  and Jelle Zijlstra). Patch by James Hilton-Balfe (Gobot1234).
- Add initial support for TypeVarLike `default` parameter, PEP 696.
  Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- Runtime support for PEP 698, adding `typing_extensions.override`. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add the `infer_variance` parameter to `TypeVar`

  runtime-checkable protocol using `isinstance()` would cause `AttributeError`
  to be raised if using Python 3.7.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.1
   ```
   - Change deprecated `runtime` to formal API `runtime_checkable` in the error
  message. Patch by Xuehai Pan.
- Fix regression in 4.6.0 where attempting to define a `Protocol` that was
  generic over a `ParamSpec` or a `TypeVarTuple` would cause `TypeError` to be
  raised. Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.0
   ```
   - `typing_extensions` is now documented at
  https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.Buffer`, a marker class for buffer types, as proposed
  by PEP 688. Equivalent to `collections.abc.Buffer` in Python 3.12. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport two CPython PRs fixing various issues with `typing.Literal`:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23294 and
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23383. Both CPython PRs were
  originally by Yurii Karabas, and both were backported to Python >=3.9.1, but
  no earlier. Patch by Alex Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the changes is that equality comparisons of `Literal`
  objects will now raise a `TypeError` if one of the `Literal` objects being
  compared has a mutable parameter. (Using mutable parameters with `Literal` is
  not supported by PEP 586 or by any major static type checkers.)
- `Literal` is now reimplemented on all Python versions <= 3.10.0. The
  `typing_extensions` version does not suffer from the bug that was fixed in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/29334. (The CPython bugfix was
  backported to CPython 3.10.1 and 3.9.8, but no earlier.)
- Backport [CPython PR 26067](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/26067)
  (originally by Yurii Karabas), ensuring that `isinstance()` calls on
  protocols raise `TypeError` when the protocol is not decorated with
  `runtime_checkable`. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport several significant performance improvements to runtime-checkable
  protocols that have been made in Python 3.12 (see
  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/74690 for details). Patch by Alex
  Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the performance improvements is that the members of
  a runtime-checkable protocol are now considered “frozen” at runtime as soon
  as the class has been created. Monkey-patching attributes onto a
  runtime-checkable protocol will still work, but will have no impact on
  `isinstance()` checks comparing objects to the protocol. See
  ["What's New in Python 3.12"](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#typing)
  for more details.
- `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable protocols now use
  `inspect.getattr_static()` rather than `hasattr()` to lookup whether
  attributes exist (backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103034).
  This means that descriptors and `__getattr__` methods are no longer
  unexpectedly evaluated during `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable
  protocols. However, it may also mean that some objects which used to be
  considered instances of a runtime-checkable protocol on older versions of
  `typing_extensions` may no longer be considered instances of that protocol
  using the new release, and vice versa. Most users are unlikely to be affected
  by this change. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport the ability to define `__init__` methods on Protocol classes, a
  change made in Python 3.11 (originally implemented in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/31628 by Adrian Garcia Badaracco).
  Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Speedup `isinstance(3, typing_extensions.SupportsIndex)` by >10x on Python
  <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `typing_extensions` versions of `SupportsInt`, `SupportsFloat`,
  `SupportsComplex`, `SupportsBytes`, `SupportsAbs` and `SupportsRound`. These
  have the same semantics as the versions from the `typing` module, but
  `isinstance()` checks against the `typing_extensions` versions are >10x faster
  at runtime on Python <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `__orig_bases__` to non-generic TypedDicts, call-based TypedDicts, and
  call-based NamedTuples. Other TypedDicts and NamedTuples already had the attribute.
  Patch by Adrian Garcia Badaracco.
- Add `typing_extensions.get_original_bases`, a backport of
  [`types.get_original_bases`](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/types.html#types.get_original_bases),
  introduced in Python 3.12 (CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/101827, originally by James
  Hilton-Balfe). Patch by Alex Waygood.

  This function should always produce correct results when called on classes
  constructed using features from `typing_extensions`. However, it may
  produce incorrect results when called on some `NamedTuple` or `TypedDict`
  classes that use `typing.{NamedTuple,TypedDict}` on Python <=3.11.
- Constructing a call-based `TypedDict` using keyword arguments for the fields
  now causes a `DeprecationWarning` to be emitted. This matches the behaviour
  of `typing.TypedDict` on 3.11 and 3.12.
- Backport the implementation of `NewType` from 3.10 (where it is implemented
  as a class rather than a function). This allows user-defined `NewType`s to be
  pickled. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Fix tests and import on Python 3.12, where `typing.TypeVar` can no longer be
  subclassed. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.TypeAliasType`, a backport of `typing.TypeAliasType`
  from PEP 695. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport changes to the repr of `typing.Unpack` that were made in order to
  implement [PEP 692](https://peps.python.org/pep-0692/) (backport of
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/104048). Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.5.0
   ```
   - Runtime support for PEP 702, adding `typing_extensions.deprecated`. Patch
  by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add better default value for TypeVar `default` parameter, PEP 696. Enables
  runtime check if `None` was passed as default. Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- The `typing_extensions.override` decorator now sets the `.__override__`
  attribute. Patch by Steven Troxler.
- Fix `get_type_hints()` on cross-module inherited `TypedDict` in 3.9 and 3.10.
  Patch by Carl Meyer.
- Add `frozen_default` parameter on `dataclass_transform`. Patch by Erik De Bonte.
   ```
   
  
</details>

</details>

author: michael-chuh
body:
Some tools get errors when kernel supports hash table batch operations and hash key or value is integer type.
`AttributeError: 'long' object has no attribute 'value'`

It's caused by ctypes library from python. For example, when hash tables try to do batch lookup, it will alloc arrays to stores keys and values first. If it is a ctypes integer type, after expanding to array, type of element will be changed to python 'long' or 'int'. When trying to access its value attribute, error message is generated.
```
  >>> from ctypes import *
  >>> a = c_uint(10)
  >>> type(a)
  <class 'ctypes.c_uint'>
  >>> a.value
  10
  >>> b = (c_uint * 1)(10)
  >>> type(b)
  <class '__main__.c_uint_Array_1'>
  >>> type(b[0])
  <class 'int'>
  >>> b[0].value
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'value'
```
Use syscount to reproduce if kernel supports hash table batch operations:
```
--- a/tools/syscount.py
+++ b/tools/syscount.py
@@ -232,22 +232,30 @@ def agg_colval(key):
     else:
         return syscall_name(key.value)
 
+# check whether hash table batch ops is supported
+htab_batch_ops = True if BPF.kernel_struct_has_field(b'bpf_map_ops',
+        b'map_lookup_and_delete_batch') == 1 else False
+
 def print_count_stats():
     data = bpf["data"]
     print("[%s]" % strftime("%H:%M:%S"))
     print("%-22s %8s" % (agg_colname, "COUNT"))
-    for k, v in sorted(data.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1].value)[:args.top]:
+    for k, v in sorted(data.items_lookup_and_delete_batch()
+                       if htab_batch_ops else data.items(),
+                       key=lambda kv: -kv[1].value)[:args.top]:
         if k.value == 0xFFFFFFFF:
             continue    # happens occasionally, we don't need it
         printb(b"%-22s %8d" % (agg_colval(k), v.value))
     print("")
-    data.clear()
+    if not htab_batch_ops:
+        data.clear()
 
 def print_latency_stats():
     data = bpf["data"]
     print("[%s]" % strftime("%H:%M:%S"))
     print("%-22s %8s %16s" % (agg_colname, "COUNT", time_colname))
-    for k, v in sorted(data.items(),
+    for k, v in sorted(data.items_lookup_and_delete_batch()
+                       if htab_batch_ops else data.items(),
                        key=lambda kv: -kv[1].total_ns)[:args.top]:
         if k.value == 0xFFFFFFFF:
             continue    # happens occasionally, we don't need it
@@ -255,7 +263,8 @@ def print_latency_stats():
                (agg_colval(k), v.count,
                 v.total_ns / (1e6 if args.milliseconds else 1e3)))
     print("")
-    data.clear()
+    if not htab_batch_ops:
+        data.clear()
```
Turn back to original ctypes type in table.py can avoid this error.

author: stephmilovic
body: ## Summary Accidentally [auto-merged an 8.9 feature](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pulls/157288) that we are putting in 8.8.1 for an evaluation. I meant to put a feature flag on it first. This is the feature flag. Sorry for the early merge! ### To test: 1. Checkout branch and run 2. Try to create a GenAI connector, note that it is not present in the connector list by default 3. Add the feature flag to dev yml `xpack.stackConnectors.enableExperimental: ['genAiEnabled']` 4. Refresh and try to create a GenAI connector, you will now be able to do so ### Caveat: If you create a GenAI connector and then disable the feature flag, it will show as a disabled connector. I think we should let this be, because to resolve we'd need to add a feature flag for the triggersActionsUi plugin and that would be 3 feature flags to turn on GenAI. If y'all are ok with the disabled connector, i think I should just leave it.

author: michael-f-bryan
body:
To future-proof the Wasmer project against new versions of webc being released, we need to make sure any code accepting a webc file as input goes through the `webc::compat::Container` type (our version-agnostic compatibility layer).

This PR updates `wasmer create-exe` and the C API to use the compatibility layer.

The `wasmer-registry` crate was also quite tightly coupled to the `webc::v1` module, but that code was only ever used by the old `wasmer run` command (removed in #3924) so I've deleted it.

body:
This PR updates [typing-extensions](https://pypi.org/project/typing-extensions) from **3.7.4.3** to **4.6.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.6.3
   ```
   - Fix a regression introduced in v4.6.0 in the implementation of
  runtime-checkable protocols. The regression meant
  that doing `class Foo(X, typing_extensions.Protocol)`, where `X` was a class that
  had `abc.ABCMeta` as its metaclass, would then cause subsequent
  `isinstance(1, X)` calls to erroneously raise `TypeError`. Patch by
  Alex Waygood (backporting the CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/105152).
- Sync the repository's LICENSE file with that of CPython.
  `typing_extensions` is distributed under the same license as
  CPython itself.
- Skip a problematic test on Python 3.12.0b1. The test fails on 3.12.0b1 due to
  a bug in CPython, which will be fixed in 3.12.0b2. The
  `typing_extensions` test suite now passes on 3.12.0b1.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.2
   ```
   - Fix use of `deprecated` on classes with `__new__` but no `__init__`.
  Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Fix regression in version 4.6.1 where comparing a generic class against a
  runtime-checkable protocol using `isinstance()` would cause `AttributeError`
  to be raised if using Python 3.7.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.1
   ```
   - Change deprecated `runtime` to formal API `runtime_checkable` in the error
  message. Patch by Xuehai Pan.
- Fix regression in 4.6.0 where attempting to define a `Protocol` that was
  generic over a `ParamSpec` or a `TypeVarTuple` would cause `TypeError` to be
  raised. Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.6.0
   ```
   - `typing_extensions` is now documented at
  https://typing-extensions.readthedocs.io/en/latest/. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.Buffer`, a marker class for buffer types, as proposed
  by PEP 688. Equivalent to `collections.abc.Buffer` in Python 3.12. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport two CPython PRs fixing various issues with `typing.Literal`:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23294 and
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/23383. Both CPython PRs were
  originally by Yurii Karabas, and both were backported to Python >=3.9.1, but
  no earlier. Patch by Alex Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the changes is that equality comparisons of `Literal`
  objects will now raise a `TypeError` if one of the `Literal` objects being
  compared has a mutable parameter. (Using mutable parameters with `Literal` is
  not supported by PEP 586 or by any major static type checkers.)
- `Literal` is now reimplemented on all Python versions <= 3.10.0. The
  `typing_extensions` version does not suffer from the bug that was fixed in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/29334. (The CPython bugfix was
  backported to CPython 3.10.1 and 3.9.8, but no earlier.)
- Backport [CPython PR 26067](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/26067)
  (originally by Yurii Karabas), ensuring that `isinstance()` calls on
  protocols raise `TypeError` when the protocol is not decorated with
  `runtime_checkable`. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport several significant performance improvements to runtime-checkable
  protocols that have been made in Python 3.12 (see
  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/74690 for details). Patch by Alex
  Waygood.

  A side effect of one of the performance improvements is that the members of
  a runtime-checkable protocol are now considered “frozen” at runtime as soon
  as the class has been created. Monkey-patching attributes onto a
  runtime-checkable protocol will still work, but will have no impact on
  `isinstance()` checks comparing objects to the protocol. See
  ["What's New in Python 3.12"](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#typing)
  for more details.
- `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable protocols now use
  `inspect.getattr_static()` rather than `hasattr()` to lookup whether
  attributes exist (backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103034).
  This means that descriptors and `__getattr__` methods are no longer
  unexpectedly evaluated during `isinstance()` checks against runtime-checkable
  protocols. However, it may also mean that some objects which used to be
  considered instances of a runtime-checkable protocol on older versions of
  `typing_extensions` may no longer be considered instances of that protocol
  using the new release, and vice versa. Most users are unlikely to be affected
  by this change. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Backport the ability to define `__init__` methods on Protocol classes, a
  change made in Python 3.11 (originally implemented in
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/31628 by Adrian Garcia Badaracco).
  Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Speedup `isinstance(3, typing_extensions.SupportsIndex)` by >10x on Python
  <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `typing_extensions` versions of `SupportsInt`, `SupportsFloat`,
  `SupportsComplex`, `SupportsBytes`, `SupportsAbs` and `SupportsRound`. These
  have the same semantics as the versions from the `typing` module, but
  `isinstance()` checks against the `typing_extensions` versions are >10x faster
  at runtime on Python <3.12. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Add `__orig_bases__` to non-generic TypedDicts, call-based TypedDicts, and
  call-based NamedTuples. Other TypedDicts and NamedTuples already had the attribute.
  Patch by Adrian Garcia Badaracco.
- Add `typing_extensions.get_original_bases`, a backport of
  [`types.get_original_bases`](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/types.html#types.get_original_bases),
  introduced in Python 3.12 (CPython PR
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/101827, originally by James
  Hilton-Balfe). Patch by Alex Waygood.

  This function should always produce correct results when called on classes
  constructed using features from `typing_extensions`. However, it may
  produce incorrect results when called on some `NamedTuple` or `TypedDict`
  classes that use `typing.{NamedTuple,TypedDict}` on Python <=3.11.
- Constructing a call-based `TypedDict` using keyword arguments for the fields
  now causes a `DeprecationWarning` to be emitted. This matches the behaviour
  of `typing.TypedDict` on 3.11 and 3.12.
- Backport the implementation of `NewType` from 3.10 (where it is implemented
  as a class rather than a function). This allows user-defined `NewType`s to be
  pickled. Patch by Alex Waygood.
- Fix tests and import on Python 3.12, where `typing.TypeVar` can no longer be
  subclassed. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.TypeAliasType`, a backport of `typing.TypeAliasType`
  from PEP 695. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Backport changes to the repr of `typing.Unpack` that were made in order to
  implement [PEP 692](https://peps.python.org/pep-0692/) (backport of
  https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/104048). Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.5.0
   ```
   - Runtime support for PEP 702, adding `typing_extensions.deprecated`. Patch
  by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add better default value for TypeVar `default` parameter, PEP 696. Enables
  runtime check if `None` was passed as default. Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- The `typing_extensions.override` decorator now sets the `.__override__`
  attribute. Patch by Steven Troxler.
- Fix `get_type_hints()` on cross-module inherited `TypedDict` in 3.9 and 3.10.
  Patch by Carl Meyer.
- Add `frozen_default` parameter on `dataclass_transform`. Patch by Erik De Bonte.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.4.0
   ```
   - Add `typing_extensions.Any` a backport of python 3.11's Any class which is
  subclassable at runtime. (backport from python/cpython31841, by Shantanu
  and Jelle Zijlstra). Patch by James Hilton-Balfe (Gobot1234).
- Add initial support for TypeVarLike `default` parameter, PEP 696.
  Patch by Marc Mueller (cdce8p).
- Runtime support for PEP 698, adding `typing_extensions.override`. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add the `infer_variance` parameter to `TypeVa

# Summary
This PR closes the sidebar immediately after a user selects a category. This will improve the user experience by reducing visual clutter and making it easier to focus on the selected category.

# Background
The current sidebar can be a source of visual clutter, especially when there are a large number of categories. This can make it difficult for users to focus on the selected category. Additionally, the sidebar can be distracting, as it can draw attention away from the main content of the page.

# Proposed Changes
The proposed changes will close the sidebar immediately after a user selects a category. This will reduce visual clutter and make it easier for users to focus on the selected category.

# Benefits
The benefits of this change include:
- Improved user experience
- Reduced visual clutter
- Increased focus on the selected category

# Implementation
The following changes will be made to implement this PR:
- The `onSelectCategory` event will be used to close the sidebar.
- The `sidebarOpen` property will be set to `false` when the sidebar is closed.

# Testing
The following tests will be used to verify the changes:
- The sidebar should close immediately after a user selects a category.
- The sidebar should not open when a user clicks on a category that is already selected.

#### Describe the solution

<!-- How does the feature work, or how does this fix a bug?  The easier you make your solution to understand, the faster it can get merged.  -->

1. Added `int_dur_faction` to Lucidity and Inner Turmoil effects so the player can tell how much longer the effect will last by number of days.
2. Fixed Inner Turmoil having a max duration of 7 hours instead of 7 days. Given each time the infighting effect triggers you get 7 hours...
3. Fixed No Ferals mod blacklisting acid zombies too for some reason.
4. Swapped the feral socialite's thompson for a repeating crossbow to match the crossbow feral, removed the violin case and gave them an empty quiver.
5. Added three more professions for the scenario: the Feral Butler/Maid is of course a player counterpart to the feral servant, the Feral Reenactor serves as this to the armored feral, and finally the Feral Chainsaw Maniac is based off another feral addition being added below as well as the lumberjack profession, 
6. Ported over a buff to the axe-wielding feral, making it a bit more of a threat in melee in exchange for lacking the ranged attack, and making its name more distinct to stand out more. Was able to implement it with more copy-from and not having to make it a full separate monster entry, my guess is they did so to override the rock-throwing attack but we can do so more easily due to the fact that all ferals have a parrot attack so we have a viable override for special attacks.
7. Also gave feral axemen a chance of dropping firefighter clothing instead of normal clothes.
8. Added feral chainsaw maniacs. Damage is scaled similarly to how the feral axeman's damage is scaled relative to a wood axe, and they get a lower melee skill due to a clumsy weapon. Their parrot attack is also more frequent and made all the time instead of at danger, to make them a noisy threat the player will hear in advance.
9. Added external tileset sprites for chainsaw ferals.
10. Added `HUMAN` flag to the following monsters, all being human-like in some way and many similar to other critters that already have the flag: experimental mutants (other, stranger mutants already get this flag), amigara horrors (because implying it may have once been a human adds a bit of weirdness to it, and adds an additional viable human target in mines alongside twisted bodies which already have the flag). Also changed grackens to give human meat when butchered and gave them the `HUMAN` flag, since they're as human-like as blank bodies which already do this. This gives science and military map extras a proper chance to have a viable target spawning in it.
11. In exchange, removed `HUMAN` flag from dementias and flesh angels, since they reanimate and yield tainted meat when butchered. Additionally set homunculi to return tainted meat on butchery and removed `HUMAN` flag from them, as they can reanimate.
12. Added the new professions to Lost and Damned scenario.
13. Added spawns of feral chainsaw maniacs, mainly to where axe ferals spawn (except `GROUP_VANILLA`) with a lower rate and always spawning a tier later (250 hours if axe ferals spawn instantly in a given area, 500 if axe bois spawn at 250).
14. Per feedback, swapped the mandatory Killer Drive trait for Psychopath so feral survivors can innately tolerate cannibalism. I'll need to remove the code effect that makes Killer Drive affect the NPC withdrawal side effect in a planned followup targeting some other code improvements.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

<!-- Explain any alternative solutions, different approaches, or possibilities you've considered using to solve the same problem. -->

I left human snails unchanged since it doesn't really say whether they're a snail that grew a human face or a human that became a snail, so left them alone for now.

Also, figuring out how to make feral socialites spawn with a posse of feral servants without them infighting with zombies is on my to-do list eventually, that will likely make the feral socialite actually solidly worth those 5 points

#### Testing

<!-- Describe what steps you took to test that this PR resolved the bug or added the feature, and what tests you performed to make sure it didn't cause any regressions.  Also include testing suggestions for reviewers and maintainers.  -->

1. Checked affected files for syntax and lint errors.
2. Load-tested in compiled build.
3. Checked that chainsaw ferals randomly pick a sprite when spawned, and have the corpse sprite assigned to them instead of the generic round dead thing.
4. Started up Lost and Damned, confirmed that the status effects show intensities indicating days left on the clock.

#### Additional context

<!-- Add any other context (such as mock-ups, proof of concepts or screenshots) about the feature or bugfix here.  -->

Axe feral change, by @Aerin-of-the-Toast https://github.com/CleverRaven/Cataclysm-DDA/pull/58028

Couldn't remember how to grab their email to co-auth it in the description and names with hyphens don't ever seem to work when trying to add co-authors in github desktop, weh. I should've set the axe feral changes aside as a different commit anyway.

author: joviel25
body:
This long PR includes the changes for the segmentation algorithm and any affected module.

The main changes related to the algorithm:
1. The processing for each slice works on the ascending and descending aorta at the same time.
2. New methods to generate the centroids to be used for processing the next slice (inspired by KMeans clustering)
3. The stop condition has changed from counting the existing pixels to checking the distance between the old and the new centroid.
4. Another stop condition is the difference in the segmented slice's intensity variance and the label image's intensity variance.

As such, the change in the 3D Slicer UI module is:
1. Added multiple parameters including:
    a. The stop limit works with the stop condition
    b. kernel size
    c. Descending aorta and ascending aorta seed in a single phase
2. Removed the old processing phase such as aorta segmentation and sagittal segmentation.

The design document has been updated based on the new changes.

author: tontonsb
body:
I've come across two common issues when working with API backends and testing the endpoints in browser or just not knowing to specify the `Accept: application/json` header. Most projects work around this by adding some middleware that either adds the header to all incoming API requests or sets a `forceJson` flag on their custom request.

This PR proposes to remedy these issues by taking a "only redirect if there's a reasonable redirect target" approach.

## Unauthenticated user

When hitting an endpoint that requires authentication, but failing the auth, user should receive an authentication error. Instead they receive a 500 error with `Route [login] not defined.` message.

**Proposed solution:** only redirect to `route('login')` if the route exists. Otherwise fall back to JSON response.

**Backwards compatibility?** Technically it is a breaking change, but I can't imagine a legit scenario where someone would rely on their auth errors being redirected to non-existant route, catching the particular error and doing some useful reporting with it.

## Validation error

When getting some request params wrong, users should see validation errors. Instead users that are hitting the endpoint in their browserse receive a redirect to `/`. Because no "previous" route exists and even if it did, Laravel wouldn't know it as the session is not enabled on API routes.

**Proposed solution:** only redirect to "previous" route if it exists in the session. Do not use `url()->previous()` as

- falling back to `url('/')` for all validation errors is unlikely to be useful in real usecases (although common in automated tests)
- redirecting to referrer would be useless as they wouldn't receive the error bag or error code in any way

**Backwards compatibility?** 

1. This will require to update web (non-json) validation tests that expect a `302` redirect now. Two options:
    - Expect `422` instead of `302`, i.e. change `assertRedirect` or `assertStatus(302)` to `assertInvalid` or `assertStatus(422)`.
    - Set up the session with the previous URL as it would be in a real life workflow. Add `session()->setPreviousUrl($prevUrl);` to the test before hitting the endpoint that should redirect you back.
2. This would also break the workflow if someone has set their index page as a dedicated error displayer. I don't know if someone actually does that. There are multiple ways to restore the previous behaviour, e.g. overriding the handler's `invalid` method or catching the exceptions in handler (and maybe just specifying `->redirectTo('/')` on them which is still respected).

This change allows building Janet from the individual source files instead of from the amalgamated `janet.c`; this considerably speeds up parallel builds on modern CPUs;

```
 make clean; time make -j NO_AMALG=0 
[...]
real	0m7.882s
```

vs

```
make clean; time make -j NO_AMALG=1 
[...]
real	0m1.481s
```

For me this make the difference between "comfortably and quickly running my tests" and "getting slightly annoyed staring at my screen",

author: catch-bull
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please review https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.rst before opening a pull request. -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

In the current push manager, push requests are only removed from the pending list when all the chunks in the push request are completed and all reply is received. This results in a high complexity for the ScheduleRemainingPushes function when there are many small objects.

This PR will remove push requests without remaining chunks from the traversal list, and every push request traversed by ScheduleRemainingPushes will have remaining chunks to be sent.

Perf Impact:

- add this test case into test_object_manager.py:
``` python
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "ray_start_cluster_head",
    [
        {
            "object_store_memory": 1 * 1024**3,
            "_system_config": {
                "object_spilling_threshold": 1.0,
                # disable unlimited
                "oom_grace_period_s": 3600,
                # force argument to be put into object store
                "max_direct_call_object_size": 512,
                "object_manager_default_chunk_size": 10 * 1024,
            },
        }
    ],
    indirect=True,
)
def test_push_large_number_and_small_size_object(ray_start_cluster_head):
    cluster = ray_start_cluster_head
    cluster.add_node(
        object_store_memory=1 * 1024**3,
        resources={"remote_node": 8},
        num_cpus=8,
    )

    def get_small_object():
        # 1KB
        return np.random.rand(1, 1024 // 8)

    TASK_NUMBER = 100
    ARG_NUMBER = 1000

    @ray.remote(resources={"remote_node": 1})
    def get_sum(ans, *args):
        for i in args:
            ans -= i.sum()
        return abs(ans) < 1e-6

    all_args = []
    all_sums = []
    for _ in range(TASK_NUMBER * ARG_NUMBER):
        data = get_small_object()
        all_args.append(ray.put(data))
        all_sums.append(data.sum())

    tasks = []
    for index in range(TASK_NUMBER):
        ans = sum(all_sums[index * ARG_NUMBER : (index + 1) * ARG_NUMBER])
        args = all_args[index * ARG_NUMBER : (index + 1) * ARG_NUMBER]
        tasks.append(get_sum.remote(ans, *args))
    assert all(ray.get(tasks))
    # Ensure that relevant logs can be printed in Raylet.
    time.sleep(10)
```
- Add the following monitoring code to count the loops inside function `PushManager::ScheduleRemainingPushes`

![image](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/assets/11995469/8cf40249-77f6-4dbd-9267-5d0cb383556b)

- run by cmd: pytest python/ray/tests/test_object_manager.py::test_push_large_number_and_small_size_object -svx

## Description

**What:** I have set the following dev flavor settings to be variables and allow them to be set with environment variables. 

- MainRegistry
- ScannerImageTag
- MainImageTag

**Why:** This is so that I customize these settings according to my development environment setup. For my specific use case, I want to point MainRegistry to my local registry so that I can easily use it with my kind cluster (very convenient), while the *ImageTags I customize them (e.g. latest) so I can ensure the images used for these components use the image builds I have run in my local development environment.

**Development Setup Goal:**
- Use a `kind` cluster as the k8s cluster with a local registry (e.g. localhost:5001
- Build central services images and push them to my local registry 
- Run stackrox operator locally, outside the cluster, and using the settings above mentioned
- Stackrox operator will reconcile a Central CR and will cause to create deployments that has images tagged as
  - localhost:5001/scanner:latest, localhost:5001/main:latest, etc...
  
I've put all these in a makefile and it works well with the changes above. It helps simplify my dev set up because I can simply build everything locally and just relaunch them as needed.

author: eob
body:
This adds a Mixin which provides official support for the notion of importing a file.

- An HTTP method is provided that just returns the (eventually content-laden) file object
- A python object method is provide which also returns the task (if there is one) upon which to wait for the content

This is a building block to making Ask My functionality something that can just be mixed-in to an AgentService.

Note:

The end-game I'm going for is a `DocumentQA` mixin which takes the service as an init arg and then applies these component-level mixins, along with a coordinating endpoint that unites them all.

body:
**Release Notes**:
``` feature operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7693 @rfranzke
The `Garden` API was extended with the new `.spec.virtualCluster.{dns,kubernetes,networking}` sections. For now, they only allow configuring the necessary information for the deployment of `kube-apiserver`. Since the API server is not deployed yet, any configuration does not have any effect. Still, you must make sure to already specify at least `.spec.virtualCluster.kubernetes.version`, `.spec.virtualCluster.dns.domain`, and `.spec.virtualCluster.networking.services`. In the upcoming releases, `gardener-operator` will also take over the management of the `kube-apiserver` deployment whilst taking the configuration into account.
```

``` breaking dependency github.com/gardener/gardener #7693 @rfranzke
The `extensions/pkg/webhook/certificates.AddCertificateManagementToManager` function does now take a list of source webhook configs instead of a single webhook config only.
```

``` breaking operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7695 @timuthy
`Seed` and `ManagedSeed` API validation has been enhanced by the following checks:
(a) New `ManagedSeed`s can only use the very same zone(s) (`managedSeed.spec.gardenlet.config.seedConfig.spec.provider.zones`) that are available in the referenced `Shoot` (`shoot.spec.provider.workers[].zones`).
(b) Existing `ManagedSeed`s can only add additional zones that are available in the referenced shoot.
(c) Removing elements in `seed.spec.provider.zones` is denied if shoots are still scheduled to the affected seed.
These restrictions were removed in Gardener `v1.60` to compensate a zone mismatch issue in Azure that is in the meantime fixed by the Azure provider extension [v1.34](https://github.com/gardener/gardener-extension-provider-azure/releases/tag/v1.34.0).
⚠️ Before upgrading to this Gardener version, please make sure to check existing `ManagedSeed` objects. They should configure as many as zone as there are available in the referenced shoot - see check (c).
```

``` breaking developer github.com/gardener/gardener #7698 @timebertt
Developers should no longer introduce new container images from Docker Hub. Please configure the [prow job](https://github.com/gardener/ci-infra/blob/master/config/jobs/ci-infra/copy-images.yaml) for copying images to the gardener GCR instead. Consult the [component checklist](https://github.com/gardener/gardener/blob/master/docs/development/component-checklist.md#general) for more information.
```

``` other operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7707 @acumino
`node-problem-detector` has been upgraded to `v0.8.13`
```

``` bugfix operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7708 @shafeeqes
A bug causing the gardenlet to be unable to access the BackupBucket generated secret in garden namespace is now fixed.
```

``` bugfix operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7710 @rfranzke
A bug has been fixed which prevented existing secrets from being adopted when they were named `kube-apiserver-etcd-encryption-key` or `service-account-key`.
```

``` other operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7714 @timuthy
Gardenlet switched from a "PodExec" based approach to calling the appropriate HTTP endpoint for initiating full snapshots. This usually takes place when the ETCD encryption key was rotated or during control-plane migration.
```

``` other user github.com/gardener/gardener #7715 @ialidzhikov
The following image is updated:
- registry.k8s.io/metrics-server/metrics-server: v0.6.2 -> v0.6.3
```

``` feature operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7729 @ialidzhikov
The `Garden` resource now supports a setting for topology-aware routing. For more details, see the [Topology-aware Traffic Routing documentation](https://github.com/gardener/gardener/blob/TBD/docs/usage/topology_aware_routing.md).
```

``` breaking operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7729 @ialidzhikov
The gardener controlplane Helm chart does no longer contain the value `global.apiserver.serviceEnabled`. `global.apiserver.serviceEnabled` is replaced by  `global.apiserver.service.enabled`. Before you upgrade to this version, please make sure that you adapt the corresponding value to its new equivalent.
```

``` feature operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7730 @rfranzke
`gardener-operator` is now managing the `kube-apiserver` instance as part of the virtual garden cluster control plane.
```

``` other operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7731 @nickytd
Now the `fluent-bit`'s output plugin targets the `logging` service instead of the previously used `loki` service.
```

``` other developer github.com/gardener/gardener #7735 @rfranzke
The server certificate of the `kube-apiserver` deployment now contains the `<service-name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local` SAN.
```

``` other developer github.com/gardener/gardener #7737 @oliver-goetz
Update local-setup to `kind@v0.17.0`.
```

``` bugfix operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7739 @timuthy
A bug has been fixed for the Gardener Operator that occasionally caused "404 not-found" errors when `garden` resources where applied and the operator ran with multiple replicas.
```

``` other operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7740 @AleksandarSavchev
Change the path of `update-local-ca-certificates.sh` script from `/etc/ssl` to `/var/lib/ssl` on our worker nodes.
```

``` other operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7741 @shafeeqes
`nginx-ingress-controller-seed` image is updated to `v1.7.0` for `1.24.x+` seeds.
```

``` feature developer github.com/gardener/gardener #7742 @plkokanov
The local deployment of Gardener is extended so that it is now possible to create a second single zone HA `Seed`. This `Seed` can be used to test the control plane migration scenario for HA `Shoot`s. Additionally, make targets were added to trigger the control plane migration integration test with HA `Shoot`s: `test-e2e-local-migration-ha-single-zone` to test the migration locally, and `ci-e2e-kind-migration-ha-single-zone` mainly intended to be used in Gardener prow jobs.
```

``` other developer github.com/gardener/gardener #7742 @plkokanov
The `register-kind2-env` and `tear-down-kind2-env` will no longer try to deploy and delete the `seed-local` `Secret`. This fixes an issue where `tear-down-kind2-env` would hang as it deletes and then waits for the `seed-local` `Secret` to be deleted which can not happen as long as the `local` `Seed` which uses it still exists.
```

``` bugfix operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7743 @ialidzhikov
A panic causing gardenlet to fail to startup when there is already a terminating Shoot namespace in the Seed is now fixed.
```

``` feature operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7746 @voelzmo
Enable memory-saver mode for the VPA recommender. It stops tracking resource consumption for Containers without matching VPAs and frees up memory.
```

``` other operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7748 @dimitar-kostadinov
The `.spec.settings.ownerChecks` field of the Seed configuration is deprecated. The "bad-case" control plane migration is being removed in favor of the HA Shoot control planes (see https://github.com/gardener/gardener/issues/6302). The field will be locked to `false` in a future version of Gardener. In this way gardenlet will clean up all owner DNSRecords. Finally, the field will be removed from the API. Set this field to `false` to be prepared for the above-mentioned locking.
```

``` bugfix operator github.com/gardener/gardener #7751 @axel7born
An issue causing an UID conflict between two Grafana dashboards is now fixed by removing the unneeded "istio-workload-dashboard.json" dashboard.
```

``` other developer github.com/gardener/gardener #7752 @oliver-goetz
Go version is updated to 1.20.3.

Annotations in `GardenletConfiguration.seedConfig.metadata.annotations` are added to the `Seed` object during registration. If an annotation is removed from `seedConfig`, it is **not** removed from the `Seed` object.

author: dongjoon-hyun
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This is a follow-up of #40922. This PR aims to add a space between `->` and value.

It seems to be missed here because the original PR already have the same code pattern in other place.

https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/74b04eeffdc4765f56fe3a9e97165b15ed4e2c73/sql/catalyst/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/sql/catalyst/expressions/ToStringBase.scala#L114

### Why are the changes needed?

**BEFORE**
```
scala> sql("select map('k', null)").show()
+------------+
|map(k, NULL)|
+------------+
|  {k ->NULL}|
+------------+
```

**AFTER**
```
 scala> sql("select map('k', null)").show()
+------------+
|map(k, NULL)|
+------------+
| {k -> NULL}|
+------------+
```

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?
Manual review.

author: jakio815
body:
This PR fixes lf-lang/lingua-franca#1777.

When the RTI `-a` option is off, and the `.lf` file's `auth=true` option is on, the RTI and federate both waits for each other's message. The previous HMAC authentication protocol started from the RTI sending a message, but I changed it to the federate sending the message to fix the problem above.

The main protocol is like the following with a 3 way handshake.
**1. FED_NONCE (Federate -> RTI)
2. RTI_RESPONSE  (RTI -> Federate) 
3. FED_RESPONSE  (Federate -> RTI)**
Details are below.

## 3-Way Handshake ##
### 1. FED_NONCE (Federate -> RTI) ###
The federate sends a FED_NONCE message to the RTI when TCP connection is established. The message is in this order:
- One byte equal to MSG_TYPE_FED_NONCE.
- Two bytes for the federate ID.
- Eight bytes for randomly created federate 's nonce.
### 2. RTI_RESPONSE  (RTI -> Federate)  ###
The RTI sends a response message to the federate. It creates its own nonce, and makes an HMAC tag using the federation ID as the key. The message is in the following order:
- One byte equal to MSG_TYPE_RTI_RESPONSE.
- Eight bytes for RTI's nonce.
- 32 bytes for HMAC tag based on SHA256. 

 The HMAC tag is composed of the following order:
- One byte equal to MSG_TYPE_RTI_RESPONSE.
- Two bytes for the federate ID.
- Eight bytes for received federate's nonce.

### 3. FED_RESPONSE  (Federate -> RTI) ###
The federate sends a response message to the RTI. It checks the received HMAC created by the RTI, and also makes a HMAC tag. The message is in the following order:
- One byte equal to MSG_TYPE_FED_RESPONSE.
- 32 bytes for HMAC tag based on SHA256.

The HMAC tag is composed of the following order:
- One byte equal to MSG_TYPE_FED_RESPONSE.
- Eight bytes for received RTI's nonce.

### RTI Check ###
The RTI finally checks the received HMAC created by the federate.

## Major changes ##
- The federate now starts the authentication.
- The first message from the federate now contains the federate's ID. Previously it happened on the second message.
- The second message from the RTI now does not contain the federate's ID.

author: prinsfrank
body:
This PR adds support for Laravel 10.

As the "2.0" branch is blocked by a partial DBAL upgrade (#538), this PR is to the "1.8" branch.

After this PR has been merged, either a "1.8.1" or "1.9" release can be tagged to add support for Laravel 10.

If you want to use this branch before this PR has been merged, you can add the repository:
```shell
composer config repositories.laravel-doctrine-orm vcs https://github.com/PrinsFrank/laravel-doctrine-orm.git
```

And then use the branch as a requirement:
```shell
composer require laravel-doctrine/orm:dev-laravel-10-support
```

If you are using other laravel-doctrine packages or other packages in general that rely on 1.x versions of this package, you can alias the development branch to the 1.9 version so this can be used in conjuction.
```shell
composer require "laravel-doctrine/orm:dev-laravel-10-support as 1.9"
```

body:
Demonstration of usage:
![image](https://github.com/shotover/shotover-proxy/assets/5120858/23ebd93b-8df3-4bf2-a1dc-55171599d2fe)


Redis benches support `shotover=none`, `shotover=standard` and `shotover=message-parsed`.

By specifying `shotover=standard|none` we include `shotover=none` and `shotover=standard` benches but exclude `shotover=message-parsed` benches.

The `|` syntax makes sense to me, its often as an "or" in the form of `||` and it also feels like its separating multiple possible values.

An alternate approach would be allowing `shotover=none shotover=standard`.
That would involve less special syntax but I think the `|` syntax is better as this approach would mess up the semantics of each key=value pair making the filter more specific.
Under this approach some key=value pairs would make the filter less specific.

author: wdonne
body:
## Description

### add-karpenter-daemonset-priority-class

When a DaemonSet is added to a cluster every node will get a new pod. There may not be enough room for this on every node. Karpenter cannot provision extra nodes just for the DaemonSet because the new pods are not scheduled the way regular pods are. It would require parallel scheduling logic that is not proper to Kubernetes. Therefore, eviction of regular pods should happen instead. This can be achieved with the priority class system-node-critical.

### set-karpenter-non-cpu-limits

For correct node provisioning Karpenter should know exactly what the non-CPU resources are that the pods will need. Otherwise Karpenter will put as many pods on a node as possible, which may lead to memory pressure on nodes. This is especially important in consolidation mode.

author: lizardqueenlexi
body:
Another big orpdate. Most relevantly, in this update I've specifically _undone_ an upstream change - the medkits were all frivolously resprited and the new ones look significantly worse than the old ones, so I put the original sprites back where they belong. Someone's gotta fight back against desaturation.

Other than that:
- Chickens will bite back if you attack them.
- Wounded people are no longer immune to wounds.
- Lightgeists are a basic mob.
- Spraycans actually work.
- Amputation actually works.
- You can put test tubes into chemistry smartfridges.
- Birdshot Xenobiology is actually powered.
- Added grilles to open spaces near Tramstation to prevent breaches from space debris.
- The UI for painting canvases now has a pixel grid to make pixel art easier.
- Elevator music is now properly confined to elevators.
- Rubber ducks now quack instead of honking (vital!).
- Air alarms have been resprited. Now you will never be able to tell that it's Space Station 13.
- Air alarms will now talk when there's a problem.
- Added three new electric-themed drinks for ethereals.
- You will get a visual alert if an IV drip is attached to you, so that you don't accidentally tear it out.
- You can revive dead potted plants by using any seed on them.
- New traitor item that lets you make fake mail for other players that can contain anything you like - whether that's bombs or contraband. Cargo techs and the QM can buy a special kit that contains a lot of these.
- Spiders have been revamped, with several new variants and other balance changes. They should make for a more interesting antag type now.
- All robotics labs now contain anesthetic tanks.
- Syndicate corpses from Legions no longer have a MODsuit or Agent ID on them.
- Snow legions spawned by portals will now drop skeletons instead of actual bodies.
- New, rare maintenance loot: the dubiously-named "spess knife", which is a swiss army knife with many different tool behaviors.
- New front-end for viewing logs.
- Resprited condiments.
- Speaking in sign language no longer revealed your identity.
- Being moved by a conveyor belt or tram will no longer make footstep sounds.
- Nearsighted prefs offers more glasses choices, and has icons.
- Admins now have a panel for managing library books.
- Fugitive hunters will now poll ghosts rather than just making a ghost spawner.
- Lots of broken access on Birdshot has been fixed.

📝  **PR Description**:

This pull request adds the long-awaited login and registration pages to our application, providing a seamless user experience and enhancing our platform's functionality.

The login page allows existing users to securely access their accounts and take advantage of all the amazing features our application offers. With this addition, users can easily log in using their registered email and password.

We've taken convenience a step further by introducing a comprehensive shopping list view. This feature dynamically generates a list of all the missing food items needed for the user's recipes. Moreover, it calculates the total price for these items, making grocery shopping a breeze.

📋 Public Recipes List:
To foster a sense of community and inspire users, we have included a public recipes list. Users can explore and discover recipes shared by other members of our platform. Each recipe includes the name and total price, giving users a glimpse into the culinary wonders created by others.

author: tombuildsstuff
body:
This PR refactors the Rest API Specs Importer such that the Terraform Acceptance Test generation now accounts for both Attributes and Blocks (and recurses these as needed). It also adds support for dynamically determining more dependent resources - notably including the Key Vault and Key Vault Key resources, which enables fixing #2549.

At this point in time this switches to outputting Terraform Variables rather than using the `locals` block - this is something we'll change in the future, but in the short-term this'll make dynamically outputting the Terraform Variables in the Terraform Generator easier.

There's more to do for this work to be usable - namely the Terraform Generator also needs updating to account for this, but since I've reworked the `testattributes` package into more granular `testing` package, this seemed like a good stopping point (which, once reviewed will need to wait for the Terraform Generator changes prior to merging).

author: tbg
body:
Backport 5/5 commits from #104133.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

Release justification: debug.zip improvement that avoids loss of observability after a recent change, and improves UX

---

This was introduced and defaulted to `false` in
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/102289.

Anecdotally I look at these in many L2 escalations[^1], and one cannot always
even change the default flag (e.g. CC), and seldom will a later debug.zip be
good enough for an RCA.

The original reason to introduce this flag seems to have been the delay
incurred when extracting these many files. There are suspicions that this
somehow exacerbates broken archives that we get from time to time, esp.
on large clusters.

This PR defaults the flag to true but also switches debug.zip so that it now
puts the ranges into a single file. This file is going to be large, but we can
handle that.

[^1]: most recently today: https://github.com/cockroachlabs/support/issues/2343#issuecomment-1569677115

Epic: none
Release note: None

body:
# Description

This PR puts the keyhashes found in votes into the `witsVKeyNeeded` set. This means adding a new UTXOW rule in Conway. Deprecated `updateTxBodyG`, since we don't use this getter in ledger anymore as Conway now uses its own UTXOW rule.

body:
Hi @Eugeny,

I found some issues about how tabby can be slow to launch in some case (#6295 , #7390 , #6253 ).
After taking a quick look, I saw that installed plugins are loaded one after another at the app startup. 

This PR aim to improve the startup time by finding and loading the plugins ~~simultaneously~~ asynchronously.

Startup on latest release with 0 plugins : ~2.9sec
Startup on latest release with 8 plugins : ~3.5sec

Startup on this PR with 0 plugins : ~2.3sec
Startup on this PR with 8 plugins : ~2.3sec

I've only have SSD so there is no huge gab on my side. (Tested on Debian 11, don't have other system on hand sorry :/)

As always, I am not sure theses changes are really relevant nor if it is a good approach to try to reduce the startup time. I hope you could give me a feedback on this when you got time :D

* [ ] all the coins are active on coinpaprika.com (please remove inactive ones)

author: lstocchi
body:
After digging a bit i found out that the node-yaml-parser is responsible of the memory leaks detected in https://github.com/vscode-kubernetes-tools/vscode-kubernetes-tools/issues/1170 . If the yaml file is not formatted correctly it start looping in a while and never ends.

It would be great to have this fixed in the lib itself but it seems an abandoned project. I opened an issue 3 years ago about another bug and nobody replied. So i guess this is a fastest solution. Maybe we should find another lib to replace this one.
https://github.com/andxu/yaml-parser

So as a temporary solution, i added another parsing using the yamljs lib. If the yaml is not formatted correctly it fails and skip the node-yaml-parser, otherwise it is called and it should not fail.

The fix can be validated by using the user example at https://github.com/vscode-kubernetes-tools/vscode-kubernetes-tools/issues/1170

body:
Steps to reproduce:

- Install Project app and activate Sub-tasks.
- Go to any project > a task > go to subtasks and add a new line.
- In the next popup, create a whole new subtask, and try to add a new property field to this subtask.

Issue:

The z-index of the properties field popup is lower than the subtask form popup, so it goes below it.

Solution:

Increasing the z-index from the `o_property_field_popover` by 100 will make it go above the subtask form popup.

author: bradmwilliams
body:
Currently the clusterbot does not provide the ability to specify environment variables to `launch` style commands.  However, we have the ability via `workflow-launch`.  This PR adds the `hypershift-hostedcluster-workflow` to the workflow config to enable users to override the default environment variables defined [here](https://steps.ci.openshift.org/workflow/hypershift-hostedcluster-workflow).

For the aforementioned story, to specify the number of worker nodes, a user can issue a command like:
`workflow-launch hypershift-hostedcluster-workflow 4.14 HYPERSHIFT_NODE_COUNT=3`
